Caraka Saṃhitā | Section on Virility

Take sprouted black gram, clean it, sweeten it, and add cooling fruits. Combine this with buffalo meat soup enriched with ghee, seasoned with yogurt and pomegranate. Add to this a paste of <term>dhānya</term> <gloss>coriander</gloss>, <term>jīraka</term> <gloss>cumin</gloss>, and <term>nāgara</term> <gloss>dried ginger</gloss>. Consumed after a meal, this preparation prevents the depletion of semen. 8
> Thus ends the virility-inducing buffalo meat soup.

One who eats fresh fish or fried <term>śapharī</term> <gloss>a type of small fish</gloss> cooked in hot ghee will not experience exhaustion during sexual intercourse. 9
> Thus ends the fish fried in ghee.

One should administer to those seeking progeny the meat of <term>rohita</term> <gloss>carp</gloss> fish, fried in ghee and cooked in goat meat soup, followed by the consumption of the remaining broth. 10
> Thus ends the preparation for promoting conception.

Minced fish meat, mixed with <term>hiṅgu</term> <gloss>asafoetida</gloss>, rock salt, and coriander, should be combined with wheat flour to bake savory cakes in ghee. In a buffalo meat broth, cook the fish until it is oily, sour, and salty. Once the broth has infused the meat, crush it and add black pepper, cumin, coriander, a small amount of asafoetida, and fresh ghee. This serves as a stuffing for the black gram cakes. These two cake preparations are aphrodisiacs that increase strength. They provide joy, good fortune, nourishment, and are supreme promoters of semen. 11
> Thus ends the two virility-inducing cake preparations.

Black gram, velvet bean, wheat, and fine rice flour ground into a paste.
